title: rwb-payment cutover load of RWB-DM-013: the handover file, the load command and its run record, a provenance column, the legacy payment_code column and the two schema-level H rows are fixed by no single source, and this slice owns no legacy criterion
source: Work Package B2-P8-007 story line (service rwb-payment, patterns DP05, DP15, DP19, acs empty, tcs TC-DM-013-01 to -04, secondary slice); Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R5.7, R7.3 and R9; legacy RWB-DM-013 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints, Permission checks, Guardrails, Test cases); TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T5.3 and Appendix T-A; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A1.4, A2.4 and A2.10; P8 context pack ownership rows
description: One combined row for the payment arm of RWB-DM-013. (1) Handover: the legacy story states only that the cutover dump is read and that the breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract; no source fixes the format, the location, the row count, the checksum, the resolution stamp or the retention of the file that rwb-source-data hands to rwb-payment, so the story names them as a design choice and holds the placeholder. (2) Invocation: the legacy story states 'No endpoint in this story' and TSD P8 appendix T-A publishes two operations, both provided; no source names the load's command, its entry point, its rights beyond the Platform administration R row, or the run record that holds its counts. (3) Provenance: the legacy guardrail requires that 'a migrated record keeps its source and its migration date', while TSD P8 T3.1 carries only DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and the standard columns of T3.0 and no column for a legacy source or a migration date, so the story places both in the standard columns and records the difference here. (4) Key: the legacy Data row keys the receipt on payment_code, while TSD P8 T3.1 carries account_payment_id as a CROSS_REF uuid and no payment_code column, and the baseline of RWB-P8-E2008-CON fixes the business key only 'where the environment grants it'; the story keeps the payment reference as the business key and writes account_payment_id only where the handover gives the ACE payment identifier. (5) Sources of the money facts: TSD P8 T3.1 names the core bank (ALS) via COLLINS as the source of amount and received_date, while the migrated amount and received date are the legacy Workbench's own recorded facts for the business date the match was decided on; the story keeps the recorded value with its provenance instead of re-reading ACE, and copies no ACE row. (6) Dependencies: the plan gives this slice an empty H row, while DP-15 names H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and DP-19 names H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the metadata row is kept exactly as the plan gives it, the sequence and the route are used and not depended on, and the deploy order behind the proceeds baseline of RWB-P8-E2008-CON is recorded in section 3. (7) Wave: the service row in Arch v5 is wave 2 and the W-MAP wave of EP08 is 4; the later wave is kept and no conflict row is needed because R5.6 rules only on a W-MAP wave that is earlier than the service wave. (8) Coverage: the plan assigns AC1 and AC3 to RWB-P1-DM013-APP and AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM013-ITG, so this slice owns no legacy criterion and carries six criteria of its own; the four legacy test case IDs are kept against them. (9) Requirement ids: the FSD 'Requirements served' table of P8 is empty and the split plan carries no requirement id, so section 18 traces to FEAT-PAY-04, FEAT-PAY-10 and the legacy key.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-013 Endpoints row 'No endpoint in this story. The migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity, and its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract.'; legacy Data row 'proceeds | id, case_id, treatment_id, payment_code, source, amount and 3 more | DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009'; legacy guardrail 'A migrated record keeps its source and its migration date, and never a copy of an ACE row.'; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 lists DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 with account_payment_id and no payment_code, and names 'Core bank (ALS) via COLLINS' as the source of DF-FIN-006 and DF-FIN-007; TSD P8 v2 T3.0 lists the seven standard columns and no provenance column; TSD P8 v2 Appendix T-A.1 lists API-P8-001 and API-P8-002, both provided; the P8 context pack lists one table (proceeds), two provided operations, the events EV-11, EV-12 and EV-25, the jobs JOB-07 and JOB-08 and no workflow, and gives the service wave as 2; the split plan gives the slice acs [] and H []; RWB-P8-E2008-CON section 12.7 fixes the business key of proceeds 'on the payment reference where the environment grants it'.
owner_role: Data steward and solution architect of rwb-payment, with the rwb-source-data owner, the schema baseline owner and the ACE team
proposed: Publish the handover file of the P1 extract with its count, its checksum and a resolution stamp per row, and name its format, its location and its retention in the Data Migration Approach; give the load a named pipeline command with its run record and its rights; add a provenance and migration-date column to the next version of the proceeds schema; keep the payment reference as the business key and settle with the baseline owner where account_payment_id is filled; keep the recorded legacy amount and received date with their provenance and copy no ACE row; record in the split plan that DP-15 and DP-19 add no H row to this slice because the sequence and the route are used and not built here; add the requirement rows of FEAT-PAY-04 and FEAT-PAY-10 to the Requirements served table of FSD P8 in its next version.
